newsitem.title: USA: Trust preferred demand strong, up to $15 bln ahead.
newsitem.headline: Trust preferred demand strong, up to $15 bln ahead.

text.p: Commerce for trust preferred paper, or capital securities, enjoyed brisk demand for the third consecutive session on Wednesday with spreads tighter by two to three basis points on a broad basis.
Bank earning reports due out starting Thursday should pave the way for more issuance of trust preferreds, possibly as high as $15 billion, said one analyst at a Wall Street investment bank.
"(New issuance) of $15 billion or $14 billion is a tall order, but can get done, and $10 billion to $12 billion is very doable, the analyst opined.
Spreads to Treasuries for trust preferreds have tightened by more than 10 basis points on the week, according to traders and analysts.

Reflecting longer term demand, Mellon Capital Trust II's $500 million of capital securities traded in a 112 bid, 109 offer market on Wednesday. The securities were issued on December 20 at a spread of 137.5 basis points over Treasuries.
Citicorp's $300 million capital securities, issued in mid-December at 120 basis points over, were bid at 104 on Wednesday.
"Demand for capital securities is powerful and it has been for a week," one trader said, adding that activity dominated the entire corporate bond arena on Wednesday.

Banks and other issuers of the securities are faced with about a four week window of opportunity to issue the securities before the Clinton Adminstration is expected to present terms of a budget proposal that either restricts or eliminates the tax-deduction on interest from capital securities.

The Federal Reserve in October ruled that bank holding companies may treat certain kinds of tax-deductable preferred stock as Tier 1 capital. Well over $10 billion in issuance of capital securities ensued.
